advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten the integration rule so bare numeric HTTP-status matches (`\b429\b`, `\b5\d{2}\b`) require status-code context (e.g. 'HTTP 500', 'status 429') instead of matching any 3-digit number.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/adapters/claude_transcripts.py:65: `r"|\b429\b"`
src/rebar/metrics/adapters/claude_transcripts.py:66: `r"|\b5\d{2}\b"`
A word-boundary 3-digit numeric match has no HTTP-status context; classify() first-match-wins means these fire on any line where env/dependency rules didn't already win.
advisory.finding: The `integration` rule's `\b429\b` and `\b5\d{2}\b` alternatives over-match: any transcript line containing a bare 3-digit number in 500-599 or the number 429 (e.g. 'ran 512 tests', 'line 523', 'commit 5ab' won't but '$500 cost', 'took 550ms') is classified as `integration`, producing spurious records.
scenarios: A transcript line mentions a duration in ms, a line number, a count, or a dollar amount in the 500-599 range or exactly 429.
advisory.suggested_fix: Anchor the status alternatives with context, e.g. `r"|(?:HTTP|status(?: code)?)\s+(?:429|5\d{2})\b"`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extract scannable text from the real Claude Code transcript schema (e.g. `message.content` content-block lists), not just flat top-level `text`/`content`, and cover it with a nested-schema test.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/adapters/claude_transcripts.py:116-121: only checks `obj.get(field)` for `field in ("text", "content")` and requires `isinstance(value, str)`, else `return raw`
scripts/backfill_transcripts.py:38: `default_dir = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/projects")` targets real Claude Code transcripts
The tests only feed flat `{"text": ...}` fixtures (test_transcript_adapter.py, test_transcript_adapter_heldout.py), so the nested-schema path is unexercised.
advisory.finding: `_line_text` extracts only a flat top-level `text`/`content` string, falling back to the whole raw JSON line otherwise. Real Claude Code transcripts (the `~/.claude/projects` default) nest message text under a `message.content` list of content blocks, so on real data the adapter scans serialized JSON (field names, roles, escaped payloads) rather than the actual message text — missing genuine signals and matching serialized structure.
scenarios: Running the backfill script against actual `~/.claude/projects` transcripts whose entries store text under `message.content` blocks.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Use a recursive glob (`rglob("*.jsonl")`) or correct the default directory so the default invocation actually discovers transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/*/`.
evidence: scripts/backfill_transcripts.py:26: `for path in sorted(Path(transcript_dir).glob("*.jsonl")):`
scripts/backfill_transcripts.py:38: `default_dir = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/projects")` — a parent dir containing per-project subdirs, not the .jsonl files directly
advisory.finding: The `backfill` glob is non-recursive (`Path(transcript_dir).glob("*.jsonl")`), but the default directory `~/.claude/projects` stores transcripts in per-project subdirectories — so invoking the script with no argument finds zero transcripts.
scenarios: A user runs `python scripts/backfill_transcripts.py` with no argument, expecting the default Claude projects dir to be mined.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that the mined record's `ts` equals the timestamp of the classified transcript entry (and "" when absent).
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/adapters/claude_transcripts.py:124-130 `_entry_ts` extracts `ts` with an isinstance guard
record built with `"ts": _entry_ts(obj)` at claude_transcripts.py:166
Tests assert only rec['kind'], rec['source'], rec['confidence'] (test_transcript_adapter.py:47-49); rec['ts'] is never asserted despite fixtures supplying distinct timestamps
src/rebar/metrics/adapters/claude_transcripts.py:97-107 `_signature` returns `match.group(0)` or `text.strip()`
record built with `"signature": _signature(text)` at claude_transcripts.py:165
No test in either file references rec['signature']
advisory.finding: No test asserts the emitted record's `ts` field is propagated from the transcript entry; the `_entry_ts` extraction (dict/str guard) could regress to always returning "" and every existing test would still pass.
merged_from: No test asserts the record's `signature` field; `_signature` returns the matched substring (with a stripped-line fallback) and a regression there is invisible to the current assertions.
scenarios: A regression dropping/mangling the timestamp goes undetected

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with a line matching two rules (e.g. env_setup + dependency) asserting the higher-priority class wins.
evidence: Comment: "Priority follows the ticket's rule ordering so that, e.g., a bare ImportError classifies as env_setup before any weaker rule can claim it" (claude_transcripts.py:26-29)
classify iterates _RULES first-match-wins (claude_transcripts.py:91-94)
Existing tests use single-signature lines only (test_transcript_adapter.py:37, test_transcript_adapter_heldout.py:41); none matches multiple rules
advisory.finding: First-match-wins rule priority is documented as load-bearing but no test exercises an ambiguous line that matches two rules, so reordering the classifier rules would not be caught.
scenarios: A line matching both a dependency and an env_setup pattern; rules reordered by mistake

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test feeding a non-JSON line containing a signature and assert it is still classified via the raw-line fallback.
evidence: claude_transcripts.py:154-158 catches JSONDecodeError/ValueError and sets obj=None, then `_line_text(None, raw)` scans raw
All test fixtures are written via `json.dumps` (_write_jsonl), so every line is valid JSON; no non-JSON line is fed
advisory.finding: The malformed-JSON fallback branch (obj=None, scan the raw line) is untested; the JSON-decode error path never executes under the current fixtures.
scenarios: A transcript line that is not valid JSON but contains an error signature must still be classified from the raw text
advisory.suggested_fix: Write a raw line like `ModuleNotFoundError: boom` (not JSON) and assert one env_setup record is produced.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add table-driven positive tests for `dependency` and `tooling` signatures asserting the expected kind.
evidence: _RULES defines dependency (claude_transcripts.py:44-56) and tooling (70-81)
Tests cover env_setup (test_transcript_adapter.py:47) and integration (test_transcript_adapter_heldout.py:47) only; no dependency/tooling assertion exists
test_enum_values (heldout:30) only checks the label set, not that these labels are ever produced
advisory.finding: Two of the four closed classifier classes — `dependency` and `tooling` — have no positive classification test; only `env_setup` and `integration` are exercised.
scenarios: A broken dependency or tooling regex silently classifies nothing
advisory.suggested_fix: Add cases such as "pip could not resolve" -> dependency and "fatal: not a git repository" -> tooling.
